clue.text: Spoiling a mother growing old

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
growing old means ageing, here spelt without the middle E

explanation.surface: A mother getting on in years is being ruined somehow.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spoiling a thing harms or ruins it, which is what a harmful influence does.

clue.text: Do secretarial work of a sort

definitions.meaning: keying letters on a keyboard is a typist's task
a sort is a kind or class

explanation.surface: Someone does office duties after a fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Typing is classic office secretarial labour, and a kind or class of thing is its sort.

clue.text: A way many may be taken back — appropriated

indicators.note: taken back tells us to read the whole run of letters in reverse order

parts.note: NE, north-east, is a compass direction, so a way to go
lots means many

explanation.surface: A route many people might retrace turns out to have been seized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken back' turns NELOTS around as one run; 'A' and 'may be' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Appropriated means taken for oneself without permission, i.e. pinched.

clue.text: Good stuff, cold remains with water!

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold on taps
ash is what remains after burning
a mere is a lake, a body of water

explanation.surface: An exclamation that fine material, chilly leftovers and water go together.
explanation.walkthrough: A MERE is a lake, a word common in English place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is a fine, luxurious wool fabric, so quality material.

clue.text: Though corrupt, no alien got a stretch

indicators.note: corrupt says the letters of the words beside it are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Despite being bent, an extraterrestrial was given a prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a stretch' looks like slang for a prison term, but it means a lengthening.
explanation.definitionFit: Elongation is the act or result of lengthening something, as when pulling it longer.

clue.text: Trendy girl and egghead are inseparable

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
her is the pronoun for a girl

indicators.note: the head of the word egg is its first letter

explanation.surface: A fashionable woman and an intellectual can never be parted.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhere is to exist permanently within something, inseparable from it as an essential quality.

clue.text: A tidy car may well gain feminine support

indicators.note: may well suggests the letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A neat vehicle might well win the backing of women.
explanation.walkthrough: A CARYATID is a pillar carved as a female figure, holding up a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A caryatid is a column sculpted as a draped woman, literally a female supporting structure.

clue.text: Worst of French tour de force

parts.note: de is the French word for of
a tour de force is a great achievement, a feat

explanation.surface: The poorest of a French masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worst' looks like a superlative adjective, but it is a verb meaning beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To worst someone is to beat them in a contest.

clue.text: Not upright like the trainee social worker

parts.note: as means like, in the same way
L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate
an ant is a worker insect living in a social colony

explanation.surface: Describing a junior social worker as not quite straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' suggests a welfare job, but it is the ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslant means at a slope or angle, so leaning rather than vertical.

clue.text: Amid the panic a messenger arrived

indicators.note: amid says the letters sit among the following words, running across them

explanation.surface: In all the confusion, a courier turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: Came is the past tense of come, a synonym of arrived.

clue.text: Having sinister propensities

parts.note: sinister suggests evil intent, but in Latin and heraldry it means on the left side

explanation.definitionFit: Sinister originally meant left in Latin, so a person favouring the left hand has sinister leanings.

clue.text: After hospital bungle dined behind a screen

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: bungle says the letters of the next word are messed up

explanation.surface: After a stay in hospital, someone botched a meal eaten out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bungle' rearranges DINED into IDDEN, which follows H.
explanation.definitionFit: Something behind a screen is concealed, out of view.

clue.text: Dear? Not up in town!

parts.note: darling means dear, as a term of endearment

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word Not is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cry of 'Dear? Not up in London!' to someone staying in the country.
explanation.walkthrough: DARLINGTON is a town in County Durham, north-east England. 'Not up' reads NOT upwards as TON.
explanation.definitionFit: Darlington is an English market town, a specific example of a town.

clue.text: Means hail-storms

parts.note: ave is the Latin greeting, a hail
rages means storms, as a temper or a gale does

explanation.surface: Hail is a type of storm, as the clue would have us believe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Means' is a noun here: arithmetic means.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics, means are mathematical mid-values, the sum divided by the count.

clue.text: A very pleasant place for fish study

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
a den is a private room for work, a study

explanation.surface: Somewhere lovely for studying fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden, like Eden, is the classic image of a delightful spot.

clue.text: Compromise to put a stop to outrage

parts.note: to end something is to put a stop to it
outrage is fierce anger

explanation.surface: Settling a dispute in order to quell public fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compromise' looks like a noun about settling, but it is the verb meaning to put at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: To compromise safety is to expose it to danger, to put it at risk.

clue.text: Help the judge to get lie in

indicators.note: in tells us the word lie is placed inside the judge's letters

parts.note: a ref, referee, is the judge in a sports match

explanation.surface: Assistance for the judge so they can sleep late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lie in' looks like a lie-in in bed, but 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief is aid given to people in need, such as food after a disaster.

clue.text: Gas that's inspired a representative

parts.note: fired means inspired, as in fired with enthusiasm
an MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

explanation.surface: Hot air from an elected politician is what got someone going.
explanation.walkthrough: FIREDAMP is the explosive methane found in coal mines.
explanation.definitionFit: Firedamp is a flammable mine gas, chiefly methane.

clue.text: Yank, a well-known architect, going over church

indicators.note: in a down clue going over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: Sir Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral

explanation.surface: An American, a famous builder, surveys a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American, but it is a verb meaning tug.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrench is to pull with a sudden twisting jerk, a hard tug.

clue.text: Touching souvenir

parts.note: a keepsake that is moving or poignant, one that brings back memories when handled or seen

explanation.definitionFit: A souvenir's whole job is to bring back memories, so it acts as a prompt to recall.

clue.text: Boy making mud-pie in tip

indicators.note: in tells us the scrambled mud sits inside the word for tip

parts.note: the end is the tip of something

indicators.note: pie, as in printer's pie, means type jumbled up

explanation.surface: A lad making mud pies on a rubbish dump.
explanation.walkthrough: A tip is British for a rubbish dump. 'pie' turns MUD into DMU, which 'in' puts inside END.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund is a male first name, standing for a boy.

clue.text: Criticise attempt to organise food-store

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Slamming an effort to set up a grocery.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry is a small room where provisions are kept, a larder.

clue.text: Sitting pretty?

parts.note: the phrase usually means being well off, but here it is sitting attractively for a portrait

explanation.definitionFit: A model sitting for an artist or camera holds an attractive pose.

clue.text: In gaming is the stuff of dreams

indicators.note: to stuff is to cram things in anyhow, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Computer games are what dreams are made of.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as held has no clear anagram signal; 'the stuff' is read as one, leaving 'of' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Imaginings are fancies and visions of the mind, like daydreams.

clue.text: The woman set about hundreds

indicators.note: about tells us the word for set goes round the other piece

parts.note: to lay is to set down
D is the Roman numeral five hundred, a number of hundreds

explanation.surface: She arranged things around many hundreds.
explanation.walkthrough: D, Roman 500, stands for several hundreds.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady is a polite term for any female person, as in 'that lady over there'.

clue.text: Absolutely the ultimate salt-shaker!

indicators.note: a shaker mixes things up, so the letters of salt are rearranged

explanation.surface: A salt cellar described as the best ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt-shaker' looks like a cruet item, but 'shaker' rearranges SALT.
explanation.definitionFit: The ultimate thing is the final one in a series.

clue.text: Points to the heart again

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north
the core is the heart of something

explanation.surface: Directions to the centre of things once more.
explanation.definitionFit: An encore is a repeat performance, a call from the audience to play once more.

clue.text: Pass an amount which appears fair

parts.note: to hand something is to pass it
some means an unspecified amount

explanation.surface: Handing over a sum that looks reasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' looks like just, but here means good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in its old sense means beautiful, as in a fair maiden.
